item.title: Voice‑Driven Coding Adds Newsletters Page to Blog with GPT‑6 Astra
item.description:
Voice‑Driven Coding Adds Newsletters Page to Blog with GPT‑6 Astra

I shipped a new feature for my blog today: the Newsletters page, which offers an index of all of the newsletters I’ve sent out, both my free weekly Substack and my monthly sponsors‑only updates.

🎙️ Voice‑Driven Development

  • Built almost entirely using my voice while cooking dinner.
  • Used the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex tab, voice conversation mode, connected to a local development environment.
  • Started the session with the command “Start dev server and open in browser”.
  • Clicked the Start new voice chat button (the one to the right of the microphone) and placed the laptop in the kitchen.
  • Model used: GPT‑6 Astra High.
  • The model replied, asked occasional clarifying questions, and edited code live.
  • Voice interaction lasted about half an hour (the time it took to cook dinner), followed by another half‑hour of typing‑based prompting to finalize the changes.

🗞️ Feature Overview

  • An index page at /newsletters/ that mixes the most recent Substack weekly newsletters and GitHub sponsors‑only monthly newsletters in reverse chronological order.
  • Year‑by‑year archive pages (e.g., /newsletters/2026/).
  • Newsletters appear on day and month archive pages but not on tag pages or the homepage.
  • Weekly Substack newsletters link back to Substack; archived monthly newsletters have their own dedicated pages.
  • Integrated with the site’s search engine.

⚙️ Technical Implementation

  • Added a new Django model and migration to represent imported newsletters, plus Django Admin configuration.
  • Created view code, templates, and import functions to populate the database from external sources.
  • Data sources imported:
    Source Import Method
    Most recent Substack items RSS
    All other Substack items Undocumented API /api/v1/archive (pagination discovered via Karen Spinner article)
    Published monthly newsletters GitHub repository simonw/monthly-newsletter-archive
    Private sponsors‑only newsletter Private GitHub repository (requires new API key)
  • Astra offered to export data for production import; I chose to keep the existing import‑script pattern.
  • After the voice session, Codex created a Git branch and opened a pull request.
  • Reviewed the PR, replaced a subprocess‑based Git call with an API‑based import using typing‑based prompts.
  • Merged the PR to deploy the feature to production.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates a complete development workflow driven largely by voice, from model definition to deployment.
  • Shows how a large language model can discover undocumented APIs, handle pagination, and generate Django code with minimal manual intervention.
  • Highlights the practicality of integrating AI‑assisted coding into everyday tasks (e.g., cooking) without sacrificing code quality.

#ChatGPT #VoiceCoding #Django #AIProductivity

Source: A new feature for my blog, built using my voice

item.title: Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS
item.description:
Google launches AI Edge Foresight, an offline‑only note‑taking app for macOS

Google has released an experimental note‑taking app called Google AI Edge Foresight that can transcribe meetings and audio files entirely offline.

🔍 Overview

  • Experimental app, free to use
  • Runs on macOS using Google’s on‑device EmbeddingGemma 2 model
  • Transcribes meetings completely offline

🧩 How it works

  • Audio is processed by an on‑device model; no cloud connection is required
  • The model runs locally on Macs with Apple Silicon

⚙️ Features

  • Offline transcription of meetings and audio files
  • Summarizes meetings while providing a space for personal notes, similar to Granola and Wispr Flow
  • Turns shorthand bullet points entered during a meeting into polished notes based on the transcript
  • Built‑in assistant lets you ask questions about the content you heard
  • Ability to connect local files for the assistant to reference when answering questions
  • Files, meeting audio, and notes never leave your computer

🚀 Availability

  • Free to use
  • Optimized for macOS on Apple Silicon Macs only

💡 Why it matters

  • Operates entirely on‑device, keeping data private
  • Provides a privacy‑focused alternative in the growing AI note‑taking market

#Google #AI #NoteTaking #macOS #Privacy

Source: Google’s AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline

item.title: Meta adds iPad support to Muse AI agent app
item.description:
Meta adds iPad support to Muse AI agent app

Meta’s Muse, the agentic AI tool that debuted on iPhone nearly a month ago, received an update that adds native iPad support.

🔍 Overview

  • Launched nearly a month ago and spent several weeks as the top free app in Apple’s App Store.
  • The latest update introduces native support for the iPad.
  • The iPad version should function similar to Muse on iPhones but better take advantage of the extra screen real estate and iPadOS multitasking capabilities.
  • iPad support is limited to a one‑line mention at the bottom of the release notes for the latest version, alongside several iPhone updates.

⚙️ New Features

  • Ability to connect Muse to additional software tools: Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Zoom, Asana, and Klaviyo.
  • New connectors for apps such as Granola and Notion.
  • Targeted at small‑business owners: users can give Muse a business goal, and the agent will autonomously plan marketing, client pitches, and develop “new product pages.”

💻 Desktop Extension

  • A Mac version of Meta’s agentic AI tool was released about a week after the original mobile version debuted, expanding usefulness to desktop tasks like organizing files.

🚀 Availability

  • iPad support is included in the latest iOS update for Muse.
  • The Mac version is already available.
  • Meta also announced a standalone Tamagotchi‑like device called the Muse Charm that runs the AI agent without a smartphone, and is working to bring Muse to smart glasses.

💡 Why it matters

  • While it took Meta 15 years to release a dedicated iPad version of Instagram, the faster turnaround for Muse’s iPad support signals strong backing for its AI initiatives.
  • Extending Muse from phone to tablet and desktop broadens its utility for small businesses and developers seeking AI‑driven productivity tools.

#MetaAI #Muse #iPad #AIagents

Source: Muse launches on the iPad

item.title: Pizza Bot Released as an Open Source, Self-Hosted AI Agent Application
item.description:
Pizza Bot Released as an Open Source, Self-Hosted AI Agent Application

Today marks the release of Pizza Bot, an open source application that runs AI agents in the background and provides them with an inbox interface. Designed to keep agents working without constant human monitoring, Pizza Bot ensures that background agents return to you only when they are finished or when they get stuck, rather than before.

🔍 Overview

Pizza Bot is a finished application built for people who need daily work done rather than for writing software. The tool originally began inside Amazon, where more than 2,000 employees utilized earlier versions for various tasks, including:

  • Meeting preparation and follow-ups
  • Email drafting
  • Slack summaries
  • CRM logging
  • Day prioritization
  • Web research

A small team rebuilt the application from the ground up as an open source project, a process made practical through the use of coding agents.

🧩 How It Works

Pizza Bot operates on an inbox model to manage background tasks. Users can initiate a task manually, set it on a schedule, or allow a webhook to start it. The interface organizes tasks using specific folders and panels:

Folder / Panel Description
Unread Completed work that you have not yet reviewed.
Action Paused work waiting on your approval or your answer.
Activity Shows work the main agent handed to a specialist, including that specialist’s own transcript.

To expand capabilities, Pizza Bot connects to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for tools, and it works with Agent Skills, which is the Markdown convention introduced by Anthropic for packaging specialist knowledge.

⚙️ Key Details

Pizza Bot is structured as both a server and a client:

  • The Server: Runs the agent, owns its state, and answers over HTTP.
  • The Client: Can be the Electron desktop application, a web browser, or a terminal.

The desktop application wraps both components, starting its own local server and connecting to it. Because the agent’s work lives on the server, a run keeps going when you close the thread, reload the page, or switch devices. A client that reconnects will catch up on what it missed.

If you host the server on an always-on machine or inside a container, you can access the same threads from a laptop, phone, or terminal. Conversely, quitting the desktop application stops its local server and ends its current runs. However, because runs are checkpointed as they go, you only lose the step currently in flight rather than the entire thread.

🛡️ Security and Compatibility

Pizza Bot is self-hosted, features no telemetry, and runs locally. Everything it stores remains in a folder you own, and the application only listens on your own machine unless you configure it otherwise. Nothing leaves your machine unless you explicitly send it there.

It allows you to choose your own model provider, with support for:

  • Anthropic
  • Amazon Bedrock
  • Google Gemini
  • OpenAI
  • OpenRouter
  • Local models through Ollama

#PizzaBot #AIAgents #OpenSource #SelfHosted

Source: Introducing Pizza Bot, an open source inbox for AI agents that work in the background | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Beyond Chatbots: How Manus AI is Redefining Autonomous AI Agents
item.description:
🤖 Beyond Chatbots: How Manus AI is Redefining Autonomous AI Agents

Summary: Discover how Manus AI is revolutionizing automation with its autonomous execution capabilities, consistently outperforming industry giants like GPT-4 in the GAIA benchmark. Learn why this breakthrough technology is set to transform business workflows and possibly replace traditional SaaS tools.

🚀 The Dawn of Truly Autonomous AI

In today’s AI landscape, most assistants operate like sophisticated search engines – they respond to queries but require constant human direction. Manus AI breaks this paradigm completely.

What if your AI assistant could take your request, develop a plan, gather necessary information, and execute the entire task from start to finish – all while you focus on other priorities? That’s the promise of Manus AI, an emerging powerhouse in the autonomous AI agent space that’s quietly outperforming industry giants in real-world applications.

📸 Imagine a visual showing the difference between traditional AI (human → AI → human → execution) versus Manus AI’s autonomous workflow (human → AI → execution).

While chatbots merely suggest, Manus AI executes. This fundamental difference represents a paradigm shift that could redefine our relationship with AI technology.

🧠 What Makes Manus AI Extraordinary?

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲

Manus AI isn’t just another language model – it’s a complete autonomous agent with impressive capabilities:

  • 🔄 Task Execution: Unlike GPT-4 which stops at generating text, Manus AI can write reports, create spreadsheets, analyze data, and even continue processing files when your device is off.

  • 🌐 Multi-Modal Processing: It seamlessly handles text, images, and code within a single framework, eliminating the need for multiple specialized tools.

  • 🔌 Advanced Tool Integration: Perhaps most impressively, Manus AI can directly interact with external applications like web browsers, code editors, and database systems – turning it into a universal automation hub.

  • 📊 Adaptive Optimization: The system continuously learns from interactions, becoming increasingly personalized to user needs over time.

𝗖𝗿𝘂𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

What truly sets Manus AI apart is its exceptional performance on the GAIA benchmark – the gold standard for evaluating AI’s real-world utility developed by Meta AI, Hugging Face, and the AutoGPT team.

While most AI systems excel at theoretical knowledge, GAIA tests practical capabilities: logical reasoning, processing diverse inputs, effective tool usage, and automating actual tasks that matter.

Here’s where things get interesting:

Model GAIA Benchmark Accuracy (%) Key Features
𝙈𝙖𝙣𝙪𝙨 𝘼𝙄 >65% (Assumed SOTA) Autonomous execution, multi-modal, tool integration
H2O.ai (h2oGPTe) 65% Enterprise-grade AI, tool-enhanced performance
Google (Langfun) 49% Advanced reasoning, limited external tool use
Microsoft (o1) 38% Open AI model with moderate capabilities
OpenAI (GPT-4o) 32% Plugin-based functionality
OpenAI (GPT-4 Plugins) 15-30% Early iteration with limited real-world performance

📸 Chart visualization comparing GAIA benchmark scores of leading AI models, with Manus AI at the top.

This isn’t just marginally better – Manus AI is reportedly doubling the performance of OpenAI’s flagship models in practical application scenarios.

🔥 Why This Matters: Industry Transformation

The implications of Manus AI’s capabilities stretch far beyond technical benchmarks. We’re witnessing the early stages of a fundamental shift in business automation:

𝙒𝙤𝙧𝙠𝙛𝙡𝙤𝙬 𝙍𝙚𝙫𝙤𝙡𝙪𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣

Traditional automation requires complex integration between multiple systems. Manus AI can serve as a universal connector, intelligently bridging gaps between different tools and processes. This means businesses can automate workflows that were previously too complex or expensive to tackle.

𝗔𝗱𝗶𝗲𝘂 𝘁𝗼 𝗦𝗮𝗮𝗦 𝗕𝗹𝗼𝗮𝘁?

Tech analysts suggest Manus AI’s comprehensive capabilities could eventually replace entire categories of software. Why maintain subscriptions to multiple specialized SaaS tools when a single AI agent can perform the same functions more fluidly?

Consider content creation: Rather than juggling between research tools, writing assistants, and design platforms, a marketing team could simply direct Manus AI to “Create a complete blog post with images about our new product features” and receive the finished asset.

𝘾𝙤𝙢𝙥𝙚𝙩𝙞𝙩𝙞𝙫𝙚 𝙇𝙖𝙣𝙙𝙨𝙘𝙖𝙥𝙚 𝙎𝙝𝙞𝙛𝙩

As Manus AI outperforms industry leaders like OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Microsoft in practical applications, we’re likely witnessing a reshuffling of the AI competitive landscape. For businesses investing in AI infrastructure, these performance differences represent massive potential efficiency gains.

🔮 The Road Ahead

While already impressive, Manus AI’s development continues with several exciting frontiers:

  • 🔗 Expanded Tool Ecosystem: Integration with more third-party applications will further extend its automation capabilities.

  • 🎯 Enhanced Multi-Modal Understanding: Improved real-time processing of images and video will enable more sophisticated visual tasks.

  • ⚖️ Ethical AI Implementation: As with any advanced AI, responsible deployment with appropriate safeguards will be crucial.

Available through manus.im, this technology appears well-positioned to lead the next wave of AI-powered productivity tools. For businesses seeking competitive advantages through automation, Manus AI represents a compelling opportunity to consolidate and streamline their tech stack.

🌟 Final Thoughts

The transition from AI assistants that merely suggest to autonomous agents that execute represents a paradigm shift comparable to the leap from flip phones to smartphones. Just as we couldn’t fully anticipate how smartphones would transform society, the full implications of truly autonomous AI agents like Manus AI are likely still beyond our immediate understanding.

What’s clear is that we’re entering a new phase of AI development where the technology doesn’t just augment human capabilities – it independently handles complete workflows. For forward-thinking organizations, the question isn’t whether to adopt autonomous AI agents, but how quickly they can integrate them into their operations before competitors do.

As we witness this transition, one question remains: How will our relationship with technology evolve when AI doesn’t just respond to our commands but anticipates and fulfills our needs?
